    • countConsistencyDefects

      @Query(nativeQuery=true) List<HoldConsistencyDefect> countConsistencyDefects(double tolerance)
      Counts, per tenant and kind, the hold_securityaccount_security rows that disagree with the ACCUMULATE and REDUCE transactions and the splits they are derived from. Read-only; nothing is repaired.

      Checked are: periods starting on a date that is neither a transaction nor a split (ORPHAN_DATE), every row's holdings against the split-adjusted signed unit sum as of that row's own from_hold_date (ROW_HOLDINGS), period chaining, the denormalised tenant/portfolio ids and the two denormalised currency pair ids. The complete expected row set is not predicted: a row is only written while the position is non-zero and same-day margin transactions collapse into one, so an absent row cannot be distinguished from a legitimately closed position in SQL. margin_real_holdings, margin_average_price and split_price_factor are out of scope because they come from the holdSecuritySplit* stored procedures.

      ROW_HOLDINGS is evaluated per row rather than on the newest row alone, because the newest row is not the final state: when a position is sold off completely the writer emits no zero-holdings row, it only closes the last one with a to_hold_date. Comparing that row against the final unit sum would report every closed position as a defect. Evaluating each row as of its own start date is correct by construction and covers every row instead of one per position.

      For the same reason PERIOD_CHAIN does not require a gapless chain ending in an open period. A closed position legitimately leaves a closed last row, and a position that is repurchased later legitimately leaves a gap between to_hold_date and the next from_hold_date. Only genuine breakages are reported: a row that has a successor while being still open, and a period that overlaps its successor.

      INVERTED_PERIOD reports a row whose to_hold_date lies before its from_hold_date. Such a row is invisible to every from <= date AND date <= to query while still carrying holdings, so it is reported on its own and excluded from ROW_HOLDINGS, where the per-row comparison would be meaningless.

      Every date comparison is made on tt_date, never on the date part of transaction_time, and matches how the rebuild keys the periods. transaction_time is a TIMESTAMP column and is rendered in the time zone of the database session, so it shifts when the database is served from a host in another zone, while tt_date is frozen when the row is written.

      The split adjustment multiplies each transaction by the product of to_factor / from_factor of every split between it and the row date, computed as EXP(SUM(LOG(...))); the factors are ratios of positive integers, so the tolerance is applied relative to the expected holdings to absorb the floating point error.

      CURRENCYPAIR compares the two denormalised currency pair ids against the pair the writer resolves for the row: the currency of the position converted into the tenant currency and into the portfolio currency, and NULL where the two currencies are equal. The comparison uses <=>, and a currency pair row that does not exist at all leaves the expected side NULL, so a dangling id is reported as well. Neither column has a foreign key, and the reporting queries join the historical rates through them, so a wrong id would otherwise convert at the wrong rate without any complaint.

      Named query: HoldSecurityaccountSecurity.countConsistencyDefects

      Parameters:
      tolerance - relative tolerance for the holdings comparison, e.g. 0.000001
      Returns:
      one row per tenant and defect kind, empty when everything agrees

    • getBuySellTransWithSecuritySplitByIdSecurityaccount

      @Query(nativeQuery=true) List<HoldSecurityaccountSecurityJpaRepository.ITransactionSecuritySplit> getBuySellTransWithSecuritySplitByIdSecurityaccount(Integer idSecurityaccount)
      Retrieves aggregated buy/sell transaction units and security split ratios for each security within the specified security custody account.
      • Filters by Securityaccount ID (?1), referencing the Securitycashaccount base entity.
      • For direct‐investment instruments (DIRECT_INVESTMENT, ETF, MUTUAL_FUND, PENSION_FUNDS): sums net units per date (positive for buys, negative for sells).
      • For margin instruments (CFD, FOREX): computes factorUnits as ±(units * assetInvestmentValue2) and retains idTransactionMargin for margin tracking.
      • Includes security split events for any traded security, computing split ratio (to_factor/from_factor).
      Results are combined via UNION and ordered by security ID and event date.
      Parameters:
      idSecurityaccount - the ID of the security custody account (Securityaccount)
      Returns:
      a list of ITransactionSecuritySplit projections with one entry per security and date

    • getBuySellTransWithSecuritySplitByIdSecurityaccountAndSecurity

      @Query(nativeQuery=true) List<HoldSecurityaccountSecurityJpaRepository.ITransactionSecuritySplit> getBuySellTransWithSecuritySplitByIdSecurityaccountAndSecurity(Integer idSecurityaccount, Integer idSecuritycurrency)
      Retrieves aggregated buy/sell transaction units and security split factors for the given security cash account and security.
      • For ACCUMULATE (4) and REDUCE (5) transactions: sums units per date, positive for buys and negative for sells.
      • For security split events: computes split ratio (to_factor / from_factor).
      The results are combined via UNION and ordered by the event date.
      Parameters:
      idSecurityaccount - the ID of the security cash account
      idSecuritycurrency - the ID of the security
      Returns:
      a list of ITransactionSecuritySplit projections with one entry per date

    • getPeriodHoldingsByTenant

      @Query(nativeQuery=true) List<IPeriodHolding> getPeriodHoldingsByTenant(Integer idTenant, LocalDate dateFrom, LocalDate dateTo)
      Retrieves daily aggregated tenant holdings for the specified tenant and date range. - Calculates aggregated values of security positions, margin gains, and market risk when all required quotes are available. - Summarizes cash deposits, dividends, interest, and fees (negated) from tenant cash account balances. - Applies currency conversion to tenant currency using historical quotes. - Includes external cash transfers to compute net gain per day.

      A day is only reported when it can be valued completely. Beside countQuotes = countSecurities, which drops a day on which a held security has no price, the query counts every hold row whose currency pair is set but carries no rate for that day, in missingFxSecurities for the security positions and in missingFxCash for the cash balances, and the two HAVING clauses remove such a day as well. The IFNULL(hqc0.close, 1) and IFNULL(hqc1.close, 1) of the conversion are therefore not a silent fallback: they apply the factor one only to a hold row that has no currency pair at all, because it is already held in the reporting currency. Neither the IFNULL nor the two counters may be removed on their own - without the counters a missing rate would add the foreign currency amount unconverted, without the IFNULL every position already held in the reporting currency would become NULL.

      Parameters:
      idTenant - the ID of the tenant
      dateFrom - the start date of the period (inclusive)
      dateTo - the end date of the period (inclusive)
      Returns:
      a list of IPeriodHolding projections with daily performance metrics

    • getZeroBaseDateByTenant

      @Query(nativeQuery=true) LocalDate getZeroBaseDateByTenant(Integer idTenant)
      Determines the zero base date of a tenant, that is the last trading day before the very first security position was opened. The period performance report treats its start date as an excluded baseline, so only a day on which nothing was invested yet yields amounts that start at zero. On the first hold date itself the opening purchase is already included, which would silently move the result of that day into the baseline. Named query: HoldSecurityaccountSecurity.getZeroBaseDateByTenant Parameters in SQL: - ?1 - the tenant, used both for the first hold date and for the cash account coverage check The candidate is taken from trading_days_plus, so it is never a weekend and never a global holiday. It additionally has to be covered by a hold_cashaccount_balance row, otherwise no baseline row could be produced for it.
      Parameters:
      idTenant - the ID of the tenant
      Returns:
      the last trading day before the first holding, or null when the tenant has no holdings at all or its cash accounts only start on or after the first hold date

    • getPeriodHoldingZeroBaseByTenant

      @Query(nativeQuery=true) List<IPeriodHolding> getPeriodHoldingZeroBaseByTenant(Integer idTenant, LocalDate zeroBaseDate)
      Produces the single baseline row of a tenant for the zero base date returned by getZeroBaseDateByTenant(Integer). Since no security was held on that day, the whole securities leg is a constant zero and the net gain collapses to the cash balance minus the external cash transfers. Cash balances, dividends, interest and fees are read from hold_cashaccount_balance and converted with the closing rate of that day exactly like getPeriodHoldingsByTenant(Integer, LocalDate, LocalDate) does, so the row can be prepended to that result without a unit break.

      The baseline row is only delivered when every cash balance of that day can be converted. The query counts the hold rows whose currency pair is set but has no rate in missingFxCash and suppresses the row when the counter is not zero, so a foreign currency balance never enters the baseline unconverted. The IFNULL(hqc1.close, 1) of the conversion therefore applies the factor one only to a cash account that has no currency pair because it is already held in the reporting currency.

      Named query: HoldSecurityaccountSecurity.getPeriodHoldingZeroBaseByTenant Parameters in SQL: - ?1 - the tenant - ?2 - the zero base date, used as the reported date and as the reference date of all hold periods
      Parameters:
      idTenant - the ID of the tenant
      zeroBaseDate - the trading day the baseline is calculated for
      Returns:
      a list with exactly one IPeriodHolding projection, or an empty list when no cash account of the tenant covers the given date

    • getMissingQuotesForSecurityByTenantAndPeriod

      @Query(nativeQuery=true) List<HoldSecurityaccountSecurityJpaRepository.DateSecurityQuoteMissing> getMissingQuotesForSecurityByTenantAndPeriod(Integer idTenant, LocalDate dateFrom, LocalDate dateTo)
      Retrieves all trading dates and security IDs for which no end-of-day quote exists for securities held by the specified tenant within the given period.
      • Scans official trading days (excluding shifted days) per security’s exchange.
      • Filters to securities actively held by the tenant in their security accounts.
      • Excludes exchanges with no market value and securities outside their active date range.
      • Identifies missing quotes where no historyquote record exists for that date.
      • Reports the currency pairs of the holdings and cash balances in the same way, since a day without an exchange rate into the tenant currency is just as unusable as one without a security quote.
      Parameters:
      idTenant - the tenant ID to scope held securities
      dateFrom - the start date of the period (inclusive)
      dateTo - the end date of the period (inclusive)
      Returns:
      a list of DateSecurityQuoteMissing projections containing tradingDate and idSecuritycurrency, where the id addresses either a security or a currency pair

    • getByISINAndSecurityAccountAndDate

      @Query(nativeQuery=true) List<HoldSecurityaccountSecurity> getByISINAndSecurityAccountAndDate(String isin, Integer idSecurityaccount, LocalDate transactinDate)
      Retrieves all hold records for a security with the given ISIN in the specified security account that are active on the provided transaction date.

      Joins the hold_securityaccount_security table with Security to filter by ISIN, and ensures the transaction date falls within the hold period (from_hold_date ≤ date ≤ to_hold_date).

      Parameters:
      isin - the ISIN of the security
      idSecurityaccount - the ID of the security account
      transactionDate - the date to check for an active hold
      Returns:
      a list of HoldSecurityaccountSecurity entities matching the criteria

    • getMissingsQuoteDaysByTenant

      @Query(nativeQuery=true) Set<LocalDate> getMissingsQuoteDaysByTenant(Integer idTenant)
      Retrieves all unique trading dates on which at least one security held by the specified tenant has no end-of-day quote. Trading days which can't used for calculation of tenants portfolio performance, because historical data for one or more security holding are not available.

      - Scans official trading days for each held security’s exchange, excluding shifted days.
      - Joins to tenant’s held securities and filters by active hold periods.
      - Excludes exchanges flagged as having no market value and securities outside their active date range.
      - Selects dates where no Historyquote record exists for the security on that trading day.
      - Adds the days on which a currency pair used to convert a holding or a cash balance into the tenant currency has no rate, because such a day cannot be valued either and would otherwise be converted at a rate of one.

      Parameters:
      idTenant - the ID of the tenant whose held securities are checked
      Returns:
      a set of trading dates with missing quotes across all held securities and their currency pairs

      @Query(nativeQuery=true) List<String> getCurrencypairsWithoutAnyQuoteByTenant(Integer idTenant)
      Returns the currency pairs referenced by the holdings of a tenant that carry no historical price at all.

      Such a pair makes every single day of the affected hold period unusable, so the period performance report finds no valid trading day left and has to tell the user which currency cannot be converted instead of returning nothing. It is the difference between a gap in the price history, which only invalidates individual days, and a currency pair that was never delivered by any connector. Named query: HoldSecurityaccountSecurity.getCurrencypairsWithoutAnyQuoteByTenant Parameters in SQL: - ?1 - the tenant, applied to both hold_securityaccount_security and hold_cashaccount_balance

      Parameters:
      idTenant - the ID of the tenant whose holdings are checked
      Returns:
      the readable names of the affected currency pairs in the form FROM/TO, sorted alphabetically, empty when every referenced currency pair has at least one price

    • getCombinedHolidayOfHoldingsByTenant

      @Query(nativeQuery=true) Set<LocalDate> getCombinedHolidayOfHoldingsByTenant(Integer idTenant)
      Retrieves all unique “combined holiday” dates for securities held by the given tenant.

      This query looks up each security’s official trading calendar, including any adjusted (minus) dates, and then filters to those dates that fall within the tenant’s active hold periods. Only exchanges with market value are considered, and results are limited to dates on or before today.

      Parameters:
      idTenant - the ID of the tenant whose held securities are checked
      Returns:
      a set of dates representing combined holiday adjustments (holdDate) for the tenant’s active holdings

    • getCombinedHolidayOfHoldingsByPortfolio

      @Query(nativeQuery=true) Set<LocalDate> getCombinedHolidayOfHoldingsByPortfolio(Integer idPortfolio)
      Retrieves all unique “combined holiday” dates for securities held in the specified portfolio.

      - Scans each held security’s official trading calendar, including any minus‐day adjustments (trading_days_minus).
      - Filters to hold periods for the portfolio (from_hold_date ≤ date ≤ to_hold_date or open‐ended).
      - Considers only exchanges with market value and dates up to today.
      - Returns each adjusted trading date (holdDate) where the portfolio holds the security.

      Parameters:
      idPortfolio - the ID of the portfolio whose held securities are checked
      Returns:
      a set of dates representing combined holiday adjustments for the portfolio’s active holdings

    • getHoldSecuritySplitTransactionBySecurity

      @Query(value="CALL holdSecuritySplitTransaction(:idSecurity);", nativeQuery=true) List<HoldSecurityaccountSecurityJpaRepository.IHoldSecuritySplitTransactionBySecurity> getHoldSecuritySplitTransactionBySecurity(@Param("idSecurity") Integer idSecurity)
      Executes the `holdSecuritySplitTransaction` stored procedure to produce a unified, chronological list of buy/sell transactions and split events for the specified security—excluding any margin trades.

      Each returned projection includes:

      • Tenant and portfolio IDs (getIdTenant, getIdPortfolio)
      • Security-account ID (getIdSecurityaccount)
      • Event timestamp (getTsDate) – tt_date combined with the time of day of the transaction, or the split date
      • Computed factor units (getFactorUnits) – total units for buys/sells or split ratio
      • Tenant and portfolio currency codes (getTenantCurrency, getPorfolioCurrency)
      • Margin-transaction ID (getIdTransactionMargin) – always null, since margin trades are omitted
      Parameters:
      idSecurity - the identifier of the security whose buy/sell and split events to fetch
      Returns:
      a list of HoldSecurityaccountSecurityJpaRepository.IHoldSecuritySplitTransactionBySecurity projections containing transaction and split details in ascending timestamp order

    • getHoldSecuritySplitMarginTransactionBySecurity

      @Query(value="CALL holdSecuritySplitMarginTransaction(:idSecurity);", nativeQuery=true) List<HoldSecurityaccountSecurityJpaRepository.IHoldSecuritySplitTransactionBySecurity> getHoldSecuritySplitMarginTransactionBySecurity(@Param("idSecurity") Integer idSecurity)
      Executes the `holdSecuritySplitMarginTransaction` stored procedure to produce a unified, chronological sequence of margin transactions and split events for a given security.

      Each returned projection includes:

      • Tenant and portfolio identifiers (getIdTenant, getIdPortfolio)
      • Security account identifier (getIdSecurityaccount)
      • Event timestamp (getTsDate) – tt_date combined with the time of day of the transaction, or the split date
      • Computed factor units (getFactorUnits) – ±(units × value) for margin trades or split ratio for splits
      • Tenant and portfolio currency codes (getTenantCurrency, getPorfolioCurrency)
      • Margin transaction ID (getIdTransactionMargin), present only for margin trades
      Parameters:
      idSecurity - the identifier of the security for which to fetch margin and split events
      Returns:
      a list of HoldSecurityaccountSecurityJpaRepository.IHoldSecuritySplitTransactionBySecurity projections containing detailed event and currency information
